paper.title_en: Variational wavefunctions for ideal anyon gas: superfluid and skyrmion Hall crystal
paper.abstract_en: The ground state of an ideal gas of anyons with statistical angle $θ\in(0,π)$ is a long-standing open problem that has gained renewed relevance with the observation of fractional Chern insulators. We construct variational wavefunctions on the sphere that incorporate the exact anyon statistics, using composite-boson, composite-fermion and parton states as starting points for neural-network optimization. For both spinless and SU(2) semions, independent constructions support a paired anyon superfluid whose energy lies well below that of the best crystal states. Liquids and crystals compete more closely for spinless anyons at $θ=π/3$. For $θ=π/3$ anyons with SU(3) flavor, we identify two competing candidates: a skyrmion Hall crystal, whose pinned flavor texture gives an integer Hall response of the anyons, and a chiral color superconductor of six-anyon clusters. This competition offers a possible explanation for the adjacent reentrant integer quantum anomalous Hall and superconducting phases in twisted MoTe$_2$. In this setting, the color superconductor has $f+if$ symmetry but differs from its BCS counterpart by 3 in chiral central charge. We also provide parameter-free analytical wavefunctions for the color-superconductor ansatz, which reach energies comparable to, or even lower than, those of the best optimized states for SU(3) anyons at $θ=π/3$ and for SU(2) semions.
